This indicates a possible pathway where gamma-Glutamylhistidine may influence the activity of the G-protein coupled estrogen receptor 1, which then modulates the activity of DNA polymerase iota. Additionally, gamma-Glutamylhistidine is also linked to another compound, 3,5-Dihydroxy-2-(3-hydroxy-2-methoxyphenyl)-7-methoxychromen-4-one, which is also a target of DNA polymerase iota. This suggests that gamma-Glutamylhistidine may have a broader impact on the activity of DNA polymerase iota through different molecular pathways. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between gamma-Glutamylhistidine and DNA polymerase iota, though further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction and the specific molecular mechanisms involved.
